iterations.planner_dissent_and_overrules: ACCEPTED from planner:iteration-1 -- (i) a pure-numpy TILED G0 FAST PATH with exact sparse fixup replaces the Numba njit kernel as the lead move: compute each tile as if every pixel were gain 0 using literally the reference expression, then overwrite the sparse non-G0 pixels wholesale, which makes byte-exactness STRUCTURAL rather than empirical and makes the reference path itself fast, so purity is satisfied trivially with no JIT inside the clock, no cache=True race across 16 Ray workers, and no float64-promotion trap; (ii) my gate had a real hole -- max|diff|==0 cannot distinguish -0.0 from +0.0 and the reference DOES emit -0.0 for masked pixels whose (adc-poff)*gfac is finite-negative, so the local gate becomes three conjuncts (NaN masks identical, bit patterns identical on the non-NaN set, signbits identical on zeros); (iii) a NULL CALIBRATION run (candidate worktree at unmodified c5ce538, so after==before) before any optimization, to validate the measurement chain and establish the ratio's noise floor; (iv) both arms become worktrees so the live tree is untouched including its __pycache__; (v) move 2 (relayout to seg,row,col,gain) DROPPED as a probable regression -- it delivers 12 useful bytes per 64 B line and streams the whole 201 MB, whereas plane-major with gathering access touches only needed lines; (vi) single-threaded pre-commitment recorded in writing BEFORE seeing any number, because at workers=1 on an exclusive 64-core node hidden threading would manufacture a fake speedup. OVERRULED: planner advised deleting worker B (moves 0+1) from iteration 1 -- I agree standalone moves 0+1 do not merit a paired job, but I did NOT convene a fourth implementation worker at all this iteration, so the point is moot rather than overruled. CORRECTIONS THE PLANNER MADE TO MY ARITHMETIC, accepted: np.select does one copyto per condition and READS EACH CHOSEN PLANE IN FULL, so the segment loop is ~2.75 GB/event not 1.9 and the per-event total is ~8.8 GB not 7.4 -- this makes 'hoisting alone cannot clear 5x' MORE robust, not less; and my 'Amdahl caps near 20x' was internally inconsistent (25 ms calib + 39 ms read against 645 is 11.7x, not 20x), so I retract the 20x figure and do not quote it.

MY OWN HEADLINE CLAIM REFUTED: C15's 'the environment degraded, we must pre-warm' is WRONG. The skeptic re-ran worker 1's unmodified read script on a fresh exclusive milano node 75 min later and got cold read 59.27 ms/event at 602 MB/s (not 3264 ms/event at 12 MB/s); sacct shows worker 1's two read jobs 34293074/34293421 and worker 2's null128 all overlapped 16:46-17:07 on the same xtc files, with the null512 slow arm in the same window -- the collapse was a SELF-INFLICTED I/O storm caused by my own parallel delegation. FURTHER: pre-warming would not have helped -- the skeptic's null re-run at the identical config 66 min later gave arm1=1.45, arm2=1.21, ratio 0.83x with the SECOND arm slower despite a warm cache, so the bias is not monotone in arm order. Null ratios now {4.31, 1.33, 5.48, 0.83}: the correct remedy is a REJECT RULE on per-arm MB_per_s plus not running competing jobs during the measurement, NOT a metric change and NOT a pre-warm. OTHER QUARANTINES ACCEPTED: (i) W1's 'tiling is 1.2-1.4x worse therefore DRAM traffic is the WRONG surrogate' is a non-sequitur and an artifact of d4.py passing non-contiguous constant slices and allocating fresh temporaries per tile (minflt 13930 -> 194644 ~= 48 ms of the 141 ms penalty); on real data with contiguous tiles the spread is +9.8%/-0.5%, and the candidate wins precisely BY moving fewer bytes, so I keep traffic as the surrogate; (ii) my 8-frame fixture UNDER-samples the hard frames -- over the harness's own 512 events the mean non-G0 is 0.2027, median 0.1134, max 0.9949, and 7.6% of events exceed the 8-frame max; (iii) the 500-700 ms sanity band could not have failed (calib_ms = 507.5 + 263.5*frac spans 508-771 for any real frame), so it was a weak test; (iv) the candidate arm's pscalib-SHA assert was downgraded to opt-in via EXP_CAND_SHA and was UNSET in all 3 runs -- exactly the check that would catch a dirty candidate tree. THE DECISIVE NEW FINDING (S3): the harness's GATE PASS does NOT check byte-exactness -- run_gate() verifies bin-key provenance, 'calib is real' (shape, some finite, not equal to raw), parallel==serial with counts exact and sums rtol, zero rescan, and import purity, but NOTHING anywhere compares calib output to a reference, and PURITY=PASS only asserts isfinite(cal).any(). A candidate that dropped masking entirely would print GATE PASS, PURITY=PASS and partition_invariant=1. So done_when item 2's three harness lines are NECESSARY but NOT sufficient, and the max|diff|==0 evidence must come from my offline bit gate run inside the candidate arm. THE GATE IS NOW ESTABLISHED AS MEANINGFUL, by the skeptic rather than by worker 3: 4 mutants of candidate.py, one anchor each -- negzero_where FAIL 20/33, float64_chain FAIL 21/33, skip_badcode FAIL 22/33 (exactly ONE pixel per frame, idx 12752948, visible only as a sign of zero), badcode_literal_zero PASS because it is semantically equivalent, pristine PASS 33/33. This independently reproduces my own finding that the bad-code mutation cannot bite and refutes worker 3's source comment claiming that multiply decides the sign of the zero. BOOKS NOW CLOSE TO 0.05%: read 38.7 + stack 10.4 + post-calib 35.3 + calib 560.9 = 645.3 ms/event against the measured 645 ms/event. So the irreducible floor is 84.4 ms/event, NOT the 79.0 I recorded (I had folded stack into read), the hard ceiling is 7.6x and the pure-numpy practical ceiling ~6.1x, and the 5.0x bar requires calib <= 44.6 ms/event = 12.6x on calib. Over the harness's actual 512-event mix the candidate is fitted at cand_ms = 28.3 + 154.2*frac => 59.5 ms => 9.42x on calib => 143.9 ms/event => 4.48x end-to-end (4.5-5.1x under floor-accounting uncertainty). CONCLUSION: the pure-numpy path alone straddles the bar and most likely falls below it; the fused kernel is load-bearing, and the remaining cost is the 154.2 ms/unit-frac gather slope on high-non-G0 frames.

Since a cold arm burns ~3.4 s/event in I/O, no candidate can beat a warm incumbent from a cold arm and any warm candidate beats a cold incumbent for free, so iteration 2 must make BOTH arms page-cache warm (pre-warm pass over the event set before the arm loop) and adopt an explicit tripwire: the two arms' MB_per_s must agree within ~15%, else the job is void.
